search_log.query: new e-paper display vendor 2026 large format colour launch 25/31 inch
search_log.notes: Saturation probe. Every name returned (E Ink, SOLUM, Samsung, InkPoster Tela 40.5in) was already in the survey.

saturation_note: Saturation reached for NEW HARDWARE VENDORS, not for deployments. The last six queries - PoE museum labels, Nordic/Baltic museum e-paper, NHS ward signage, Korean-language large colour e-paper, generic 2026 large-format launches, and APAC/Middle East integrators - returned only names already in the survey (E Ink, Samsung, LG, SOLUM, Visionect, TintTech, Artec, MpicoSys, Papercast, InkPoster). Notably, the query designed to re-run the exact Artec Design precedent ('Power over Ethernet e-paper museum exhibition labels') returned Artec, TintTech, Visionect and MpicoSys and nothing else - the museum seam that produced the original breakthrough is now mined out. The genuinely new hardware names this sweep produced - Luminator, GDS and, at the component level, the corroborated E-Paper Innovation panels - all came from TRANSPORT and INDUSTRIAL channels, not from museums. The one channel that is NOT saturated is non-English search: the single Japanese-language query was the most productive of the sweep, and Chinese-language searching produced the Guangzhou OED find in an earlier sweep. Deployments remain far from saturated - every vendor case-study page fetched yielded new named installations, and that supply is effectively unlimited. COUNTING NOTE: new_vendor_count = 48 is the number of company names surfaced this session that do not appear anywhere in the nine prior sweep outputs (checked programmatically against a 499-name index built from every prior devices/vendors/search_log entry). Only 12 of those 48 were substantive enough to profile in the vendors array; the rest are signage-software companies, room-booking SaaS, mounting and distribution channel, or regional AV integrators with no verified e-paper hardware. The honest new-to-known ratio for names that actually touch >=13in e-paper HARDWARE is about 3 new (Luminator, GDS, and the corroborated E-Paper Innovation panel line) against roughly 30 known - a low yield that is itself the saturation evidence. Names I initially believed were new but which the index showed were already captured: CREA, DNP/Dai Nippon Printing, Frame Labs, Densitron, Galari, SonicGrace, Digital Signbox, Orient Display, Ynvisible, Praevar and Aluratek.

vendors.name: AMSYS Innovative Solutions (AMLABEL)
vendors.country: United States (Houston, Texas area implied by the MFA Houston partnership)
vendors.corporate_form: Private company; AMLABEL is described as an AMSYS Innovative Solutions company
vendors.hardware_track_record: AMLABEL museum gallery labels built on Visionect e-paper, deployed at the Museum of Fine Arts Houston; project started 2013, product shown at MW2016 and awarded a 2016 thought-leadership award
vendors.abandonment_history: Unknown - the public trail is heavily weighted to 2016-2017 and I found no recent activity, which is itself a mild warning sign
vendors.rationale: An integrator, not a manufacturer, and only at 6in and 9.7in. Included because it is the clearest documented museum-label integrator in North America and shows the pattern: a small integrator wraps someone else's panel in a vertical-specific CMS.

leads_not_followed.lead: Nooka Art's 'Light Dynamic Wave' e-paper installation in a ribbon window at the Taipei Dome
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: A second architectural-scale ART installation on e-paper, in Asia, by a studio nobody in this survey has looked at. Surfaced only in a search summary; I never fetched a page about it, so it is unverified. Worth one fetch of Nooka Art's own site.

leads_not_followed.lead: 3Form's 'Viva' architectural material co-developed with E Ink
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: An architectural-materials company embedding e-paper into panels. If e-paper is being sold as an interior surface rather than a screen, that is a different procurement channel with different sizes.

leads_not_followed.lead: Review Display Systems' actual e-paper product catalogue
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: Their claim of 32in e-paper modules with bespoke firmware and APIs is the single most interesting integrator claim found. Their own product URL 404'd. A direct enquiry would settle whether a UK integrator will build a custom colour e-paper display with a local API.

leads_not_followed.lead: CREA's 42in EPS pricing and whether they will export outside Japan
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: CREA is the only vendor found with HDMI input plus SD card plus FTP on a 42in e-paper panel. Everything about the architecture fits; the unknowns are price, export, and whether the s-color line will ever reach 42in.

leads_not_followed.lead: Guangzhou OED's 31.2in colour e-paper at 18fps entering mass production
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: A non-E-Ink colour electrophoretic panel at 30in+ would be the first real price competition in the category. Known vendor, but the mass-production claim from March 2025 was never followed up to see if it shipped.

leads_not_followed.lead: Whether Philips Tableaux's Android SoC will run a sideloaded app
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: If it will, a 32in Spectra 6 colour panel becomes drivable from a self-hosted server with no PPDS cloud - which would change the answer for this project. The Institut Pasteur deployment proves third-party software (Telelogos) can drive it.

leads_not_followed.lead: E Ink Prism / Prism 3 availability to non-automotive, non-architectural buyers
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: Prism is the only E Ink product line with a documented history of being used for actual commissioned artwork (DAZZLE, BMW NOSTOKANA). It is a segmented film, not an image display, so it cannot show a painting - but it is worth knowing whether E Ink still sells it at all.

leads_not_followed.lead: Heureka Science Centre (Helsinki) and the National Museum in Krakow as TintTech references
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: Two more museum deployments of the PoE + self-hosted-CMS architecture. They appeared in search summaries of TintTech material but not on the references page I fetched.
